title: Keep adult controls off the learner's screen
statement: Keep what is meant for adults, such as timers, build strings, counters and skip or review switches, off the learner's screen.
detail: The reading project's QC checklist makes it a blocking rule that timers, build strings, counters, scripts and skip controls appear only in the preview mode, and its attention standard keeps them to the preview or the end-of-lesson receipt (`grade3-reading/artifacts/AlphaRead-QC-Checklist-v2-2026-09-04.md`; `grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/process/ATTENTION-HIERARCHY.md`). The checklist flagged a switch to the review view in the student page, warning that if it stayed every gate would be one tap from skippable, and a UI review agent later found that unlabelled switch on staging and on production: one tap put a child in the review view, where every gate opens (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-argus-ui-2026-09-30/REGISTER.md`). The fix renders the switch only once a page is already in review mode or a staging flag turns it on (the same register).

evidence.quote: Timers, build strings, counters, scripts, skip controls in previewer (?review=1) only; student DOM greps clean
**Metadata lives with adults.** Grade/build strings, timers, page counters, scripts, skip controls: previewer (`?review=1`) or the receipt only.
if it stays, every gate is one tap from skippable
toggle renders only after `?review=1` (mode already review)
The reviewer component loads conditionally and never mounts in student mode.
If you can see timers, page counters, or Skip, you are in the wrong app. Stop. Most of one review round described previewer-only chrome.
I’ll separate the review notes from the student experience and send a revised offline ZIP.
Where we broke this rule we say so — the progress bar shows a raw *"18 / 46"* to students, against our own design note.
